summary: Frontend-only regression test of the /menu page performance fix (loading='lazy' + whileInView reveal). Tested on desktop (1920x800) and mobile (390x844) with realistic incremental mouse-wheel scrolling. All 41 menu-item cards render correctly - above-the-fold cards are fully opaque at load, off-screen cards animate in as scrolled into view, and none get permanently stuck at opacity 0. viewport={once:true} confirmed - cards stay visible after scrolling back to top. Native lazy loading confirmed (only 1 image fetched at initial load, the above-fold Tacos Builder image; the rest fetch on-demand as scrolled near). Regression checks all pass: cat-nav chip click smooth-scrolls & reveals target section, add-to-cart increments cart badge, Tacos Builder modal opens correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: Menu.jsx: whileInView + viewport={once:true, amount:0.2} is correctly applied to both Tacos Builder wrapper and MenuItemCard wrappers. Delay formula `Math.min((i % 6) * 0.05, 0.3)` is a good bounded stagger.
MenuItemCard.jsx & TacosBuilderCard.jsx: loading='lazy' decoding='async' correctly added; browser confirms only above-fold imgs fetched at load.
Minor observation (pre-existing, not part of this fix): a couple of item images 404 in the network tab (seed-data gap already documented in PRD).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Menu page perf/reveal-animation fix verified end-to-end on both desktop and mobile. 41 total cards across 9 French-language categories (signatures, classiques, smash-burgers, wraps, sandwiches, sides, kids, desserts, drinks). All whileInView animations trigger reliably on real incremental scroll. Note category slugs are English (cat-signatures, cat-drinks, etc.) even though labels are French. Some menu-item images 404 due to pre-existing seed gap - unrelated to this fix.
rca of the issue: N/A - no regression found. The fix (loading='lazy' + whileInView with amount:0.2) works correctly. The earlier ambiguity from the main agent's instant JS scrollTo() jumps was because instant synthetic jumps sometimes race IntersectionObserver's scheduling; real incremental scroll (mouse.wheel with 180ms waits per 400px step) reliably triggers all reveals as expected.
